Many are decorated in a warm Japanese tone, with a private balcony, kitchen, fridge, and microwave built in · Rooms start at around THB 1,200/night, with a real guest score of about 8.2 — worth a look if you're after a quiet stay with plenty of private space in Phayao.

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — In the shortest possible summary, Zen Home Resort & Garden @ Phayao is a small resort for people who want "a house of their own" rather than a regular hotel room · It isn't a hotel block in Phayao town, and it isn't a lakeside resort selling Kwan Phayao views · Instead it's a small Japanese zen-style garden resort of around 9 rooms whose main selling point is roomy, house-like rooms with a living area and in-unit kitchen, set in the Mae Ka Subdistrict on the University of Phayao side · The resort has been open since 2023, so it's fairly new, and one thing many reviews mention is that the owner is a University of Phayao lecturer who comes down to run it personally · Real guest reviews line up on who fits here: families who want plenty of space and a kitchen to cook in, couples after quiet and privacy, parents dropping off or visiting students at the University of Phayao, and people staying long-term in this area · If your plan is mainly to wander and eat in town or stay by Kwan Phayao, this may not be the right location, since it's a fair way from the town center · It's a place that plays the "private space and quiet" card well at an affordable price, and it's clearly a different option from the usual Phayao stay.

Location and getting around — You need to understand the location before booking, because it's both the draw and the thing to weigh up · The resort sits at 224 Moo 1, Ban Mo Kaeng Thong, Mae Ka Subdistrict, Mueang Phayao District, the southern side of the province, next to the University of Phayao zone · The closest landmark is the University of Phayao, just about 2 kilometers away, or a 5-minute drive, with the PJ Market in front of the university, restaurants, cafes, and convenience stores of the student area scattered around · Phayao town and Kwan Phayao, the province's highlight, are about 18–20 kilometers away, or roughly a 25–30 min drive · This is why many reviews note it's "far from the town center and Kwan Phayao," which is a fact you should be aware of · Anyone driving their own car will have the easiest time, using the resort as a base to run into town or out to spots around the lake, with free parking on-site · But people without their own car should be prepared, because Mae Ka isn't an area where everything is within walking distance, and calling a public taxi or motorbike taxi into town may be inconvenient and add cost · If your main goal is the University of Phayao or a quiet getaway, this location works; but if you intend to visit the lake and town every day, plan your travel time carefully.

"The room is huge, with a separate living area and an in-unit kitchen, like staying in Japan. The garden setting is quiet and zen, and the staff look after you so warmly it feels like family. The room is new and clean, and the price is worth the space you get."

Room types and decor — Zen Home has around 9 rooms in total, which makes it small and very private · What sets it apart from the usual Phayao stay is that several of its rooms are houses or cottages that are several times bigger than a standard hotel room · They range from queen-bed rooms for couples or two people, to one-bedroom cottages, to two-bedroom houses that fit a whole family · Many come with a separate living area, in-unit kitchen, large refrigerator, and microwave, making it easy to cook simple meals or reheat your own food — something families and long-stay guests love · The decor is a warm Japanese style, leaning on woodwork, natural tones, and a simple zen feel · Every room has air conditioning, a 32-inch LED TV with satellite channels, a desk, a minibar, a private bathroom, and many have a private balcony looking out over the garden · Reviews consistently praise the rooms as very clean, new, and bigger than expected at this price, with comfortable beds and a quiet, relaxing in-room feel — more like a holiday house than a hotel · Some reviews also mention snacks and ready-to-eat food set out in the fridge, a small touch that makes it feel as warm as staying at a relative's place.

Facilities and the garden setting — To be straight from the start, Zen Home has no swimming pool and isn't a resort you come to for luxury facilities · Its selling point is a quiet zen-style garden setting and private space rather than activities or big-resort facilities · On-site there's a shaded, Japanese-styled garden, sitting corners, and a quiet atmosphere genuinely suited to relaxing · The basic facilities you'd expect at a place this size are all here: free Wi-Fi in all rooms, free parking, a 24-hour front desk, daily housekeeping, and a shared kitchen and washing machine · What many people point to as the charm is its "resort-grade homestay" feel, with the owner and team looking after you closely · As for the pool, anyone set on swimming should understand before booking that there isn't one here, because the resort's concept centers on quiet and private space · Overall, measured on "atmosphere for the price" Zen Home does well in its own way, but measured on the sheer number of facilities, set your expectations correctly: this is a quiet garden-house stay, not a full-activity resort.

Food and the in-unit kitchen — Food at Zen Home needs a clear explanation, because the information differs from platform to platform · Some channels say a simple breakfast is included with the room, and some reviewers mention a "simple but complete breakfast" and snacks prepared in the fridge · while other platforms say there's no breakfast service or full restaurant · This difference probably depends on the room type and the time of booking, so if breakfast matters to you, check directly with the resort before booking whether your chosen room includes it · But what makes food here more flexible than elsewhere is the in-unit kitchen many rooms have, along with a large refrigerator and microwave — many guests buy ingredients or ready-made food from the PJ Market and shops in front of the university and cook or reheat it in their room, which is both cheap and very convenient for families or long stays · For main meals, the Mae Ka area near the University of Phayao has a decent choice of student-area restaurants and cafes a short drive away · Overall, food at Zen Home isn't something you come for at the resort itself, but the kitchen gives you the flexibility to handle your own meals easily.

Service — Service is the area where Zen Home earns the most consistent praise in real reviews · Many voices agree that the staff are attentive, warm, and as friendly as family · What makes the service feel special is that the resort is run by the owner, a University of Phayao lecturer, with the university's student interns helping out · Many reviews praise the intention and enthusiasm of the student staff looking after guests; while it isn't always as polished as the professionals at a big hotel, you get sincerity and care in return · There's a 24-hour front desk, daily housekeeping, and a team happy to recommend places to visit or eat in the area · For the sake of honesty, since this is a small and fairly new resort, some of the service may not be as systematic as a chain hotel, but in terms of warmth and close, personal care it's a strength many guests are impressed by and mention first.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — Pulling together Agoda, Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and Wongnai, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: house-like rooms with a living area and in-unit kitchen, pretty and quiet Japanese zen decor, new and clean rooms, a private garden setting, warm family-like care from the staff and student interns, and good value for the space you get · Many say it feels more like staying at a Japanese-style house than a typical provincial hotel · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is the location far from the town center and Kwan Phayao, about 18–20 kilometers — inconvenient without a car · Next is that at times the resort still looks like it's under construction or not fully finished in some corners, since it's a fairly new place still being developed; the lack of clarity over whether breakfast is included in some rooms; and the absence of a swimming pool for those expecting one · These criticisms are mostly about setting expectations and choosing a location that matches your trip's style, rather than problems with room quality or service.

"Loved the quiet and the private space — great for a family getaway, with a kitchen to cook your own meals, and the student staff who look after you are really dedicated · The only downside is it's far from the town center and Kwan Phayao; without a car it's a bit of a hassle."

Price and value comparison — Zen Home's starting price is around THB 1,200/night in the normal range, climbing to roughly THB 1,500–2,500+ for the larger houses or two-bedroom houses over long weekends · Compared with Phayao stays in the same price band, many are standard-sized hotel rooms, but Zen Home gives you much more space, plus a living area and in-unit kitchen — which, if you count space and function for the price, is good value for families or groups who need room · Another saving is the in-room kitchen, which lets you cook or reheat your own meals and cuts dining-out costs noticeably over multiple nights · That said, you have to factor in the "location cost" — if you need to go into town or out to Kwan Phayao every day, the fuel or travel cost of an 18–20 kilometer round trip is a hidden expense · In short, if your focus is the University of Phayao area or a quiet getaway with plenty of space, Zen Home offers good value; but if your focus is touring the town and the lake, the value drops because of the long travel.

Good to know before booking — A few things make a stay at Zen Home go more smoothly · One, be clear on the location: the resort is in the Mae Ka area near the University of Phayao, about 18–20 kilometers from the town center and Kwan Phayao, and best suited to people driving their own car · Two, if you want a room with an in-unit kitchen and living area, specify a house or cottage type when booking, because not every room is the same · Three, check breakfast clearly before booking — whether your chosen room includes it — since the information differs across platforms · Four, there's no swimming pool here, so if you're set on swimming, choose somewhere else · Five, since it's a new resort still being developed, some corners may not be fully finished, so set your expectations on the roomy, clean rooms and the quiet atmosphere first · Six, if you're dropping off or visiting a University of Phayao student, this location is the most convenient, just about 2 kilometers away · Seven, check-in is from 2:00 PM, check-out before 12:00 PM, and there's free parking on-site.

The bottom line — From all the real reviews, Zen Home Resort & Garden @ Phayao is the best fit for people who want a roomy house with an in-unit kitchen, in a quiet Japanese-style garden setting near the University of Phayao, at an affordable price · House-like rooms with a living area and kitchen, relaxed zen decor, privacy, and warm owner-run service make it a clearly different option from the usual Phayao stay · If your trip is about visiting family studying at the University of Phayao, a quiet family getaway, or a long work stay where you want a kitchen and private space — this place fits just right · But if you intend to tour Kwan Phayao, the town, Wat Si Khom Kham, or the lakeside walking street every day and don't have your own car, it may be too far out, and you should consider a stay in town or by the lake instead · Overall, Zen Home is a small resort that does what it sets out to do well — selling space, quiet, and warmth rather than location and full facilities — and that's why the right kind of guest rates it as a memorable Phayao stay.

honestSummary: Zen Home Resort & Garden @ Phayao is a solid pick for people who want a roomy house with an in-unit kitchen, in a quiet Japanese-style garden setting near the University of Phayao — new, clean rooms, plenty of privacy, and warm owner-run service at an affordable price · It isn't a luxe lakeside resort, has no swimming pool, and sits about 18–20 km from the town center, but for a quiet getaway, a student visit, or a family who wants their own space and kitchen, it fits just right.
honestChecks: If you intend to tour Kwan Phayao and the town every day — the resort is in the Mae Ka area about 18–20 km from the town center (a 25–30 min drive) → best for people driving their own car; without one, choose a stay in town or by the lake instead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Zen Home Resort & Garden @ Phayao

faq.q: Where is Zen Home Resort & Garden @ Phayao, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 224 Moo 1, Ban Mo Kaeng Thong, Mae Ka Subdistrict, Mueang Phayao District, in the University of Phayao area · just about 2 km from the University of Phayao (a 5 min drive), but about 18–20 km from the town center and Kwan Phayao (a 25–30 min drive) · There's free parking, and it's best suited to people driving their own car · Those without a car may find it inconvenient, since it's outside the area you can walk around.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Zen Home, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around THB 1,200/night in the normal range · There are several layouts, from queen-bed rooms and one-bedroom cottages to two-bedroom houses · The resort has around 9 rooms, many of them roomy houses with a living area and in-unit kitchen · Prices depend on the season and room size, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Do the rooms at Zen Home really have an in-unit kitchen, and is it good for families?
faq.a: Yes · the highlight here is that many rooms are roomy houses or cottages with a separate living area, in-unit kitchen, large refrigerator, and microwave, so you can easily cook or reheat your own food — great for families, groups, and long stays · But not every room is the same, so specify a house or cottage type when booking if you want an in-room kitchen.

faq.q: Does Zen Home have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool — the resort focuses more on quiet and private space in a Japanese garden style · As for breakfast, the information differs across platforms and rooms: some rooms have a simple breakfast and snacks in the fridge, while some channels say there's none → check directly with the resort before booking, or it's easy enough to cook your own in the in-room kitchen.

faq.q: Who is Zen Home good for?
faq.a: It suits families who want plenty of space with a kitchen, couples after quiet and privacy, parents visiting or dropping off University of Phayao students, and people on long stays in the Mae Ka area · It feels more like staying at a Japanese-style house than a hotel · If you intend to tour Kwan Phayao and the town every day and don't have a car, a stay in town or by the lake may suit you better.

faq.q: What's the review score for Zen Home, and what are the criticisms?
faq.a: The average from real reviews is around 8.2 out of 10 (Agoda around 8.2 from about 90 guest reviews · TripAdvisor and Wongnai rate it well) · Frequent praise covers the roomy rooms with an in-unit kitchen, the quiet Japanese garden setting, new and clean rooms, and the warm care from staff and student interns · Common criticisms include being far from the town center and Kwan Phayao, inconvenient without a car, some corners not fully finished as it's a new place, and no swimming pool.
